artworks.title: Midas Washing at the Source of the Pactolus
artworks.description: Poussin's Metropolitan canvas shows the Phrygian king scrubbing the golden curse from his hands in the Pactolus. Ovid's remedy made landscape: desire rinsed into a river that will run with gold dust.

artworks.title: Midas and Bacchus
artworks.description: In the Bavarian State collections, Poussin stages Midas before Bacchus — the mortal king begging release from the gift that starves him. The golden touch as a theological bargain, not a fairy-tale joke.

artworks.title: Apollo as Victor over Pan
artworks.description: Jordaens' Prado contest paints Midas among the judges who prefer Pan's pipes to Apollo's lyre — and earn the donkey ears. The Phrygian king as bad critic: taste punished in fur and long ears.

artworks.title: King Midas
artworks.description: Tournier's half-length Midas wears the ass's ears as royal attribute — the king who judged the music contest wrong, fixed in Caravaggesque light. Punishment become portrait.

artworks.title: The Punishment of Midas
artworks.description: Régnier shows Apollo fastening the donkey ears on Midas after the verdict for Pan. The golden-touch king here is pure hubris of judgment — ears as the visible price of preferring the wrong music.

films.title: The Golden Touch
films.description: Disney's Silly Symphony restages the golden touch as a cartoon caution — Midas starving amid gold he cannot eat.

music.title: Le Jugement de Midas
music.description: Grétry's opéra comique restages the music contest — Midas prefers Pan and Marsyas to Apollo, and earns the donkey ears on a Paris stage.

popCulture.title: Midas touch
popCulture.description: English still calls a gift for making money the Midas touch — the Phrygian king's blessing rewritten as a business compliment.

popCulture.title: Midas
popCulture.creator: Mary Shelley
popCulture.description: Mary Shelley's verse drama (with lyrics by Percy) binds the golden touch to the donkey-ear contest — Romantic satire of greed and bad judgment.
